title: The Third Founding Declaration
author: https://hedgehogreview.com/contributors/james-davison-hunter
text:
In the annals of history, modern democracy stands out as one of humanity’s greatest achievements. From its beginnings, democracy was an exercise in hope—hope that the world and the lot of ordinary people could be made better. This was especially true in America, a nation predicated solely on the ideal of expanding freedom, equality, justice, and toleration rather than on established traditions, inherited identities, or long-standing territorial boundaries. The hope of America was for a home and a shared endeavor where Americans of all backgrounds could flourish. Both flawed and incomplete in its implementation, democracy in America—civic, pluralist, and liberal—has nevertheless stumbled forward in its history toward the realization of that ideal.

Today, however, American democracy faces its greatest crisis since the American Civil War. The signs are everywhere: extreme partisanship making political compromise impossible, increasing threats and acts of political violence, a loss of trust in all branches of government and all major institutions of civil society, and a growing disregard for the rule of law by a leadership class often defined by corruption and cowardice. These are some of the forces that today undermine the rich legacies of freedom for which Americans have sacrificed, fought, and died, forces that would ultimately pull the nation into tyranny.

Too many Americans today believe that the cause of this crisis lies in the malice of the “other side.” While active political harms are inflicted by actors across the political spectrum, the sources of our crisis trace to sources of disaffection and disempowerment with origins far deeper in American history and culture. These sources have weakened the ethical ideals, moral dispositions, and social habits that comprise America’s true constitution, one etched within the deepest aspirations of its citizens rather than merely written on parchment or graven on tablets of marble or brass.
